newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Q2 GDP decline linked to soft demand.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Q2 GDP decline linked to soft demand.

text.p: The Swiss Federal Statistics Office said weak demand was a key factor in a 0.9 percent drop in the country's second quarter gross domestic product.

"While consumption in private households recovered from a decline in the second half of 1995, and investments in fixed assets continued to maintain a certain dynamic, the other aggregates of total demand, as well as imports, showed declines," the Statistics Office said.
It said that positive developments in some areas, including services, helped to push consumption in private households higher.

But in the goods sector, purchases were slack. The Statistics Office cited declines in spending on clothing and household furnishings. With respect to holiday spending, a shift continued to foreign countries, but to a lesser extent in the second quarter than in 1995, it said.
It noted that the second quarter data showed exports falling for the first time in three years. Imports also fell for the first time in three years, it said.
The price index remained unchanged over a year, "a phenomenon which was last registered at the end of 1976 to the start of 1977", the Statistics Office said.
According to data released by the Statistics Office, the second quarter GDP, reported on an annual, seasonally adjusted basis versus the previous quarter, showed its sixth consecutive decline.
Based on a comparison of the same quarter of the previous year, the GDP fell 0.5 percent in the second quarter, for a fourth consecutive decline.
